title: Fix fallback to OpenGL3 from Vulkan initialization on Android.
body:
This PR addresses a problem where the existing fallback path for Vulkan failing to initialize on Android doesn't work as intended.

It can be quite difficult to follow the initialization order on Android, so the key part here is that operations happen in this order.
- Main::setup
  - Features rendering driver picking, but no DisplayServer initialization.
  - Under normal circumstances, setup2 is called directly here, except for iOS and Android.
- GodotLib.getRendererInfo (Java)
  - Queried by the Java code that creates the Window.
  - The Window type and associated libraries are created here based on the current rendering driver.
  - The Window type also checks for Vulkan library support on its own.
- Main::setup2
  - Creates the DisplayServer.
  - DisplayServerAndroid actually has a GLES3 fallback implemented if Vulkan fails to initialize. However, this will not work if the Java side has created a surface with a different type.

Basically, unless both the Java side and the C++ side happened to land under the same API, the fallback will just not work.

The workaround is a bit ugly as it involves having to use a global variable for the DisplayServer's Vulkan context instead, but I believe it should be safe as using multiple DisplayServers is not really expected as it relies on the Singleton pattern a lot.

Fixing this fallback allows us to introduce mechanisms such as a ban list for certain GPUs from picking Vulkan, which will be a follow-up PR to this one.

To test this out, you might have to force the Vulkan Context initialization to fail (rendering_context_driver_vulkan.cpp). There are multiple conditions it could fail from, but I don't have a device which currently supports Vulkan but fails to initialize. However, that doesn't mean that it couldn't happen for a multitude of reasons. By forcing the initialization to fail, I've verified this PR works properly in my Pixel 8 and it manages to switch to OpenGL3 without much issue.

The PR also removes `Main::get_rendering_driver_name()`, which seems to be a leftover from times where it was not possible to just query the OS for this information instead, if my understanding of it is correct. Tracking the driver at the level of Main requires the setup process to constantly update the string in case the OS has changed it.
